entries.name: aiogram
entries.use_for: Build Telegram bots in Python with a fully async framework.
entries.why: Popular async Telegram framework with FSM, routers and middlewares.
entries.summary: aiogram is a fully asynchronous Python 3.10+ framework for the Telegram Bot API, built on asyncio and aiohttp. Its API bindings are code-generated so they track new Bot API versions quickly. It provides an update router, a finite state machine, magic filters, middlewares, webhook replies and gettext/Fluent i18n.
entries.best_for: Building Telegram bots in async Python, especially ones needing conversation state (FSM), routing and middlewares.
entries.not_for: Developers new to asyncio; the README strongly advises prior asyncio experience. Telegram-only, so not for multi-platform chat bots.

entries.name: Baileys
entries.use_for: WhatsApp Web API over WebSockets, no browser needed
entries.why: Most used unofficial WhatsApp library for Node that needs no Puppeteer
entries.summary: TypeScript library using WebSockets to talk to the WhatsApp Web API without a browser. Version 7.0.0 introduced breaking changes; an example script demonstrates common use cases and a new guide is at baileys.wiki.
entries.best_for: WhatsApp automation in Node without Puppeteer overhead.
entries.not_for: Production use needing official support: it is unofficial, risks account bans and breaks when WhatsApp changes; use the official WhatsApp Business API for compliance.

entries.name: Bolt for JavaScript
entries.use_for: Build Slack apps and bots that handle events, commands and interactivity.
entries.why: Slack's official app framework; handles auth, events and Socket Mode.
entries.summary: Slack's official JavaScript framework for building Slack apps. Handles authentication, events, commands and interactivity, and supports Socket Mode and HTTP receivers.
entries.best_for: Slack bots and apps in Node.js/TypeScript.
entries.not_for: Other chat platforms (see Chat SDK) or Python stacks (use Bolt for Python). Requires a Slack app and tokens.

entries.name: Bolt for Python
entries.use_for: Build Slack apps in Python
entries.why: Official Slack framework for Python
entries.summary: Slack's official Python framework for building Slack apps with the latest platform features. Supports sync and async apps and listeners for events, commands and interactivity.
entries.best_for: Python-based Slack bots and apps with first-party support.
entries.not_for: Other platforms or JavaScript stacks; requires Slack app credentials. Requires Python 3.7+ per README.

entries.name: Chat SDK
entries.use_for: Write a bot once and deploy to Slack, Teams, Discord, Google Chat and more
entries.why: Unified TypeScript bot SDK from Vercel
entries.summary: Unified TypeScript SDK to build chat bots once and deploy to Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Chat, Discord, Telegram, GitHub, Linear, WhatsApp and more via adapters. Features event handlers (mentions, reactions, buttons, modals), AI streaming and pluggable state such as Redis.
entries.best_for: Multi-platform bots, especially AI agents, sharing one codebase across chat services.
entries.not_for: Single-platform bots needing every platform-specific feature, where official SDKs go deeper; adapters may not expose all capabilities.

entries.name: discord.js
entries.use_for: Build Discord bots in Node.js.
entries.why: The most used Discord library, with full API coverage and active maintenance.
entries.summary: Node.js module for the Discord API with full API coverage. The monorepo includes discord.js plus tooling such as create-discord-bot and other packages.
entries.best_for: Discord bots in JavaScript or TypeScript with the biggest community.
entries.not_for: Other languages, or lightweight HTTP-only interaction bots; the library is feature-rich and can be heavy for tiny bots.

entries.name: Discord.Net
entries.use_for: .NET wrapper for the Discord API
entries.why: Most popular C# Discord library
entries.summary: Unofficial .NET wrapper for the Discord API, split into NuGet packages for REST, WebSocket, webhooks, commands and interactions.
entries.best_for: C# Discord bots with slash command and interaction services.
entries.not_for: Non-.NET stacks; being unofficial it may lag API changes. Pick packages deliberately.

entries.name: discord.py
entries.use_for: Build Discord bots in Python with an async API.
entries.why: The most popular Python Discord library, with slash commands and extensions.
entries.summary: Async Python library for the Discord API with support for slash commands, extensions and optional voice (discord.py[voice]).
entries.best_for: Python Discord bots with a mature, widely used library.
entries.not_for: Non-async code or non-Python stacks; voice needs the voice extra and extra dependencies.

entries.name: grammY
entries.use_for: Build Telegram bots in TypeScript on Node, Deno, Bun or serverless.
entries.why: Modern, well-documented Telegram framework with a rich plugin ecosystem.
entries.summary: Telegram bot framework for TypeScript running on Node, Deno, Bun or serverless. Provides middleware, filtered handlers such as bot.on('message:text'), long polling or webhooks, and a plugin ecosystem with documentation.
entries.best_for: Modern Telegram bots in TypeScript across multiple runtimes.
entries.not_for: Python or other language bots; Telegraf is an alternative with a more established userbase.

entries.name: Koishi
entries.use_for: Cross-platform chatbot framework with a plugin ecosystem
entries.why: Popular multi-platform bot framework
entries.summary: Koishi is a cross-platform, extensible chatbot framework written in TypeScript. It ships a web console with an online plugin market so bots can be set up and extended without coding, and supports QQ, Telegram, Discord, Feishu and others with multi-account, cross-platform data. Over 3000 official and community plugins exist, with hot module reload for plugin development.
entries.best_for: Running or developing chat bots across several platforms (especially QQ and other Chinese platforms) with a console UI and a large plugin ecosystem, in TypeScript/Node.js.
entries.not_for: Readers who need English documentation; the README and much of the ecosystem are in Chinese. Not for Python-based bot stacks.

entries.name: LangBot
entries.use_for: Build LLM-powered bots across Discord, Slack, Telegram, LINE, WeChat
entries.why: Production IM bot platform with agent/knowledge-base orchestration and a plugin system across many chat platforms.
entries.summary: Open-source platform for building LLM-powered instant-messaging bots across Discord, Slack, Telegram, LINE, WeChat and more. Provides agent and knowledge-base orchestration, a plugin system and a management UI; cloud option available.
entries.best_for: Connecting LLMs and agents to chat platforms with a ready platform rather than SDK code.
entries.not_for: Custom bot logic in code or only one platform, where a platform SDK is simpler; it is a full platform to deploy.

entries.name: NoneBot2
entries.use_for: Async cross-platform chatbot framework for QQ, Telegram, Discord and more.
entries.why: One plugin system across many chat platforms via adapters.
entries.summary: NoneBot2 is a cross-platform, extensible Python chatbot framework built on type annotations and asyncio. It talks to existing protocol adapters for different chat platforms and handles the events they deliver, with 100% type-annotation coverage. The nb-cli scaffold creates and runs projects, and a plugin store offers official and third-party plugins.
entries.best_for: Building async Python chat bots that target multiple platforms through adapters, with a CLI scaffold and plugin ecosystem.
entries.not_for: Getting a platform's protocol implemented: NoneBot2 only consumes existing adapters. Docs and community are primarily Chinese. Not a drop-in replacement for NoneBot1.

entries.name: pyTelegramBotAPI
entries.use_for: Simple Python library for the Telegram Bot API, sync and async.
entries.why: Easy to start with and widely used; GPL-2.0 licensed.
entries.summary: Simple, extensible Python implementation of the Telegram Bot API, both synchronous and asynchronous. Tested on Python 3.11-3.15 and PyPy 3.
entries.best_for: Quick Telegram bots in Python with a low learning curve.
entries.not_for: Strict-typed, router-heavy or FSM-focused designs (aiogram) and GPL-2.0 compatibility concerns for closed-source code.

entries.name: python-telegram-bot
entries.use_for: Async Python wrapper for the Telegram Bot API
entries.why: The most popular Telegram bot library
entries.summary: python-telegram-bot is a pure-Python, asynchronous interface to the Telegram Bot API for Python 3.10+. Besides the raw API it provides shortcut methods and high-level classes in telegram.ext for building bots, with webhook and polling support and full static type hints. Releases are signed with sigstore.
entries.best_for: Writing Telegram bots in Python with a well-documented, typed library that covers the full Bot API plus a high-level application framework.
entries.not_for: Projects that cannot accept the LGPLv3 license or need other chat platforms. Pre-3.10 Python versions are not supported.

entries.name: Serenity
entries.use_for: Rust library for the Discord API
entries.why: Leading Rust Discord library
entries.summary: Rust library for the Discord API with event handler traits and a Client builder. For slash/text commands the README points to the poise framework; for voice to songbird.
entries.best_for: Discord bots in Rust with strong type safety.
entries.not_for: Quick command-framework bots, where poise (built on serenity) is the recommended layer; Rust learning curve.

entries.name: Telegraf
entries.use_for: Build Telegram bots in Node.js with a middleware-based API.
entries.why: Established Telegram framework with full Bot API typings.
entries.summary: Telegram Bot API framework for Node.js in JavaScript or TypeScript with middleware, filters and typings. README states full Bot API 7.1 support and webhooks via http, fastify, Connect or Express.
entries.best_for: Node.js Telegram bots with middleware style.
entries.not_for: Newer Bot API features beyond 7.1 or multi-runtime (Deno/Bun) use; grammY is a more recent alternative.

entries.name: Telegram Bot SDK (PHP)
entries.use_for: Build Telegram bots in PHP, with Laravel integration.
entries.why: Most used PHP Telegram SDK.
entries.summary: PHP SDK for the Telegram Bot API with Laravel integration out of the box.
entries.best_for: Telegram bots in PHP, especially inside Laravel apps.
entries.not_for: Non-PHP stacks; check maintenance and Bot API version coverage in the docs before relying on newer features.

entries.name: Telegram.Bot
entries.use_for: .NET client for the Telegram Bot API.
entries.why: The standard C# Telegram library, kept current with Bot API releases.
entries.summary: Most popular .NET client for the Telegram Bot API, published as NuGet packages by the Telegram Bots team. It points to WTelegramClient for the Client API.
entries.best_for: C# and .NET Telegram bots kept current with Bot API releases.
entries.not_for: User-account automation (it uses the Bot API only, not the Client API); other languages.

entries.name: TelegramBots (Java)
entries.use_for: Build Telegram bots in Java.
entries.why: The standard Java Telegram library, with a Spring Boot starter.
entries.summary: Java library for Telegram bots supporting both webhooks and long polling (long polling recommended). Includes example bots and a Spring Boot starter.
entries.best_for: Java Telegram bots, including Spring Boot setups.
entries.not_for: Non-JVM stacks, or very new Bot API features; check release state of the current version.

entries.name: whatsapp-web.js
entries.use_for: Automate WhatsApp through WhatsApp Web from Node.js.
entries.why: Most used WhatsApp Web client library; unofficial, so check WhatsApp terms before production use.
entries.summary: Node.js library that automates WhatsApp Web through Puppeteer, exposing most web client features as an API in a managed browser instance.
entries.best_for: Prototyping WhatsApp bots and automations in Node with broad feature access.
entries.not_for: Production or compliance-sensitive use: it is unofficial and can violate WhatsApp terms; Puppeteer makes it heavy. Use the official WhatsApp Business API instead.

entries.name: whatsmeow
entries.use_for: Go library for the WhatsApp web multidevice API
entries.why: Robust Go WhatsApp library used by Matrix bridges
entries.summary: Go library for the WhatsApp web multidevice API. Supports sending and receiving text/media messages, groups, invite links, typing and read receipts, app state sync and retry receipts.
entries.best_for: WhatsApp bots and bridges in Go (used by Matrix bridges).
entries.not_for: Official or supported integrations: unofficial, can break and risks bans; non-Go stacks.
